title: Against Celsus, Book V
blurb: Origen answers Celsus’s claim that no God or Son of God has come down to men, shows why Christians worship God alone and not angels or the stars, and defends the hope of the resurrection against the charge that it is “the hope of worms.” He then rejects Celsus’s case that each nation should keep its own ancestral laws, and answers his mockery of the angels at Jesus’ tomb and of the many Christian sects.
first_english_note: Earlier English: Frederick Crombie (Ante-Nicene Fathers, 1872) and Henry Chadwick (1953). This is a fresh English translation from Koetschau's Greek; neither was used as wording.

text_history.method: Copy-text: Paul Koetschau's Greek, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI. All 65 chapters of Book V were translated from the Greek in two passes (a literal gloss with key Greek words, then reading English), and every clause was then checked against the Greek in a separate review. Doubtful readings in the Greek are recorded in the translator's notes.
